newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - IBM SEES LOCAL SALES EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - IBM SEES LOCAL SALES EXPANSION.

text.p: Computer giant IBM says it sees plenty of room to expand its presence in Lithuania's infant information technologies market.
"Since 1992, our sales have been increasing by 35 to 40 percent per year and we see a lot more potential here," Valdas Monkus, IBM's country manager in Lithuania, told Reuters in a recent interview.

Monkus declined to give specific figures but said that IBM computers had about eight to ten percent of the local market share and hoped to muscle out the "no-name" computers which currently have the lion's share of sales.
"Our industrial sector is still far behind Western Europe in terms of computerization and we see lots of potential there," he said.
"The Mazheikiu Nafta oil terminal has invested millions of dollars in our information technologies and we hope to get other big clients in the energy sector," he said.
Monkus also said that the government, which must operate in a tight fiscal environment, has been unable to afford large-scale computerization but would have to in the future.
Monkus said that one local company, Sigmanta, was importing parts for power personal computers from IBM and assembling them for resale in Lithuania.
But IBM's immediate plans in Lithuania were to focus on sales and not manufacturing, he added.
